Addresing Members of the Council at Ahmadu Bello International Conference Bauchi, Governor Bala Mohammed urged them to convince electorates through peaceful engagement and effective communication by highlighting the laudable projects and achievements recorded by the APM-led administration across the state.
He expressed confidence in the ability of the party’s candidates to emerge victorious in all elective positions and called on supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation efforts.
Bala Mohammed therefore announced plans for a massive empowerment programme targeting thousands of youths, women, traders and artisans across Bauchi State to improve livelihoods and economic opportunities.
The Governor appreciated the APM for providing a political platform at a challenging period in the PDP, describing the opportunity as significant for their political future.
Speaking on behalf of members, the Chairman of the State APM Campaign Council, Alhaji Hamza Koshe Akuyam who described APM as the most popular political party in the state, challenged candidates of other political parties to present verifiable records of their achievements to the electorate. He stressed the need for members to work collectively to ensure that the all candidates of Allied Peoples Movement APM secure victory at all levels in the 2027 general elections.
… Lauds Military’s Efforts In Combating Insecurity, Approves Land For Armoured Corps Training Centre
Governor Bala Abdulkadir Mohammed has approved land allocation for the establishment of a Nigerian Army Armoured Corps training facility in Bauchi State, following a request by the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu.
The approval was granted during a courtesy visit by the Army Chief and members of the Nigerian Army High Command at Government House, Bauchi. The Governor directed the Commissioner for Lands to work with a military officer designated by the COAS to identify a suitable location for the facility.
Governor Bala described the military’s contributions to maintaining peace and security in the state as significant, while commending President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the Chief of Army Staff for establishing two new Army battalions in Alkaleri and Tafawa Balewa Local Government Areas. He noted that the swift deployment of troops and logistics had made both formations operational within a short period.
He identified banditry, kidnapping and illegal mining, particularly across Alkaleri, Toro, Tafawa Balewa, Bogoro and Katagum, as emerging security threats. He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to providing logistical, intelligence and operational support to security forces, as well as assisting families of fallen military personnel.
Earlier, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu said his visit was to attend the grand finale of Exercise Mugun Bugu 2026 in Alkaleri and the maiden Nigerian Army Armoured Corps Reunion and Pulling-Out Ceremony, expected to attract more than 100 retired senior officers.
He described Exercise Mugun Bugu as an annual military exercise that consolidates the Nigerian Army’s various training programmes, while appreciating Governor Bala for his continued support to the Armoured Corps and other military formations.
The COAS explained that Bauchi plays an important role in the professional development of Armoured Corps personnel, adding that the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to twelve divisions has increased the need for dedicated training infrastructure, hence the request for a permanent training facility in the state.
